system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | 20% of price / **AUD 4.8m**, said to be final and agreed. | **25% / AUD 6m**. The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying the draft; none exists. | **Reject and counter at AUD 6m** — the asserted principal-level agreement is unsupported and cannot substitute for the required approval. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only excess recoverable. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000 tipping basket**, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject and restore buyer thresholds** — Seller’s proposal materially suppresses valid claims and converts the agreed tipping basket into a deductible. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General claims: **18 months**; Seller also seeks to apply limitations to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24 months** for general warranty claims only. An 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost’s prior written approval; none exists. | **Reject and reinstate 24 months** — 18 months is unauthorised, and general limitations must not spill into separate claim categories. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate regime: **100% cap**, at least **six years**, and outside the general de minimis, basket and knowledge bar. | **Reject outright** — ownership, capacity and title risk cannot be reduced to the general warranty regime. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims, with no stated fraud exception. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance**, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert an express overriding carve-out** — this protection is non-waivable under the buyer playbook. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; no deemed disclosure by data room, register or prudent search. | **Delete general/deemed disclosure and require specific disclosure** — document dumping does not give the Buyer adequate notice of warranty exceptions. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion; any knowledge qualifier should use named seller knowledge persons subject to reasonable enquiry, and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Delete clause 8.3 as drafted** — it improperly imputes adviser and constructive knowledge and would undermine disclosure and due diligence protections. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours only; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are met. | A Completion condition requiring **effective Bluefen consent and evidence that all associated conditions are satisfied** before Completion. | **Strengthen the condition precedent and prohibit deemed satisfaction on delivery** — Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and conditional consent may be ineffective. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; security release will be provided after Completion. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases of all security at Completion. Any later release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Require payout and releases through the Completion funds flow** — an unsecured promise of post-Completion release leaves the acquired group exposed to debt and encumbrances. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 bonuses are said to be a Seller matter but are omitted from the funds flow; on-costs are unaddressed. | Express seller funding or a specific funds-flow item for **AUD 420,000 plus all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs**. | **Add a specific seller-funded adjustment/payment mechanism** — omission risks the Company bearing a Completion-triggered Seller liability after Completion. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 remains recorded as open without independent verification or confirmatory assignment. | Broader indemnity covering losses arising from failure to obtain or perfect ownership/use of the relevant IP, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure; do not accept AUD 180,000 as verified. | **Broaden the indemnity and require payment/assignment evidence** — paying an unverified fee alone may not secure or cure the required IP rights. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; investigation is incomplete and no confirmed access, breach, notification duty or loss exists. | Preservation of logs and evidence, continued investigation, prompt updates, Buyer participation where appropriate, and protection for resulting liabilities without assuming any breach or quantum. | **Add investigation, preservation and reporting covenants and reserve remedies** — the current facts are inconclusive, so neither materiality nor liability should be predetermined. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals are characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Further assessment of timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and avoidability; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction. | **Keep under diligence and make no automatic adjustment yet** — the disclosure does not establish whether the AUD 330,000 is ordinary, accrued, unavoidable or terminable. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General caps and limitations are intended to apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Separate treatment for Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities, without hidden override by the general warranty regime. | **Rewrite the limitation architecture with express category-specific rules** — the Seller’s catch-all wording could silently erode separately negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the internal DD-012 share register as evidence of ownership of 100% of the shares. | Independent evidence of ownership, authority and absence/release of encumbrances, including appropriate corporate searches, original records/instruments and completion deliverables. | **Do not accept DD-012 as conclusive** — a company-maintained register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof of good and unencumbered title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Says Tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax and IP terms expressly **open**, separately negotiated and appropriately ring-fenced; make no assumption of unlimited liability or final resolution. | **Reject the claimed settlement and reserve both categories** — the playbook records no agreement on Tax/IP allocation or liability limits. |
=== END ADVICE ===
